name: Brewed Coffee (drip/filter)
notes: USDA SR Legacy 'Beverages, coffee, brewed, prepared with tap water' (FNDDS 2710375 identical). Per-100 g = per-100 mL (density ~1.00). Caffeine varies widely: McCusker et al. 2003 (J Anal Toxicol 27:520) measured 58-259 mg per 16-oz specialty coffee (~12-55 mg/100 mL), and the same Starbucks Breakfast Blend ranged 259-564 mg/16 oz over six days; Starbucks currently publishes ~310-315 mg per grande Pike Place (~66 mg/100 mL). USDA's 40 mg/100 mL (~95 mg per 8 oz) is a typical home-brew value. Range upper bound set to 70 to cover large chain brews; extreme outliers exist. UK CoFID 'coffee, infusion, average' cross-check: ~2 kcal/100 g, consistent.

name: Decaf Brewed Coffee
notes: USDA SR 'coffee, brewed, prepared with tap water, decaffeinated'. Decaf is NOT caffeine-free: McCusker et al. 2006 (J Anal Toxicol 30:611) found 0-13.9 mg per 16-oz cup in 10 outlets (0-2.9 mg/100 mL); Starbucks brewed decaf 12.0-13.4 mg per 16 oz.

name: Espresso (single shot)
notes: USDA SR 'coffee, brewed, espresso, restaurant-prepared' (FNDDS 2710378 identical): 212 mg caffeine/100 g (~64 mg per 30 mL shot). Shots vary by dose, volume and chain: McCusker 2003 measured 75.8 mg in one shot and 140.4 mg in two short shots at a US shop; Starbucks publishes ~75 mg per shot; per-volume concentration therefore ranges roughly 150-300 mg/100 mL (ristretto is more concentrated, lungo less). Serving conventions: Italy/EU single ~25 mL, US single ~30 mL (1 fl oz), double/doppio ~60 mL.

name: Espresso (double shot / doppio)
notes: USDA SR 'coffee, brewed, espresso, restaurant-prepared' (FNDDS 2710378 identical): 212 mg caffeine/100 g (~64 mg per 30 mL shot). Shots vary by dose, volume and chain: McCusker 2003 measured 75.8 mg in one shot and 140.4 mg in two short shots at a US shop; Starbucks publishes ~75 mg per shot; per-volume concentration therefore ranges roughly 150-300 mg/100 mL (ristretto is more concentrated, lungo less). Serving conventions: Italy/EU single ~25 mL, US single ~30 mL (1 fl oz), double/doppio ~60 mL. Same per-100 mL data as single; only the default serving differs.

name: Decaf Espresso
notes: USDA SR lists only 1 mg caffeine/100 g, but McCusker et al. 2006 measured 3.0-15.8 mg per 1-oz decaf shot at Starbucks (~10-53 mg/100 mL). The default keeps USDA's value; the range warns that real decaf shots can be meaningful for caffeine-sensitive users.

name: Caffè Americano

source.name: Derived: USDA espresso (FDC 171891) diluted; caffeine from Starbucks published grande value

notes: Derived entry: espresso nutrients scaled for 3 shots (90 mL) in a 473 mL drink (Starbucks grande build), rest water. Caffeine uses Starbucks' published 225 mg per grande (47.6 mg/100 mL); USDA espresso maths gives ~40 mg/100 mL, consistent. Shot count per size varies by chain (tall 2, grande 3, venti 4 at Starbucks; many cafés use a double in 240-350 mL), so caffeine per 100 mL ranges ~25-70.

name: Cold Brew Coffee (ready to drink)

source.name: Derived: USDA brewed coffee nutrients (FDC 171890); caffeine from Starbucks published value; range from Fuller & Rao 2017

notes: No USDA record for cold brew. Nutrients use brewed coffee as proxy (black cold brew ~5 kcal per 16 oz per Starbucks). Default caffeine = Starbucks grande cold brew 205 mg/473 mL (43.3 mg/100 mL); Nitro grande ~280 mg. Lane et al. 2017 reported ~207 mg per 12 oz (58 mg/100 mL) for a commercial cold brew. Fuller & Rao 2017 (Sci Rep 7:17979) brewed at 1:10 coffee:water and measured 990-1230 mg/L (99-123 mg/100 mL), vs 840-1060 mg/L for hot brew at the same ratio: cold brew is not inherently stronger; its caffeine depends on the grind:water ratio and dilution. Undiluted concentrates should be diluted ~1:1 or logged with a custom caffeine value.

name: Iced Coffee (brewed, over ice)
notes: FNDDS 'Iced Coffee, brewed' - values are lower than hot brewed coffee because the recipe includes melted ice. Unsweetened, black.

name: Caffè Latte
notes: FNDDS 'Coffee, Latte' (unsweetened, cow's milk; FNDDS default milk is reduced-fat). Per-100 g converted with density 1.03 g/mL. Caffeine 36 mg/100 g is taken from the sister FNDDS records (Latte nonfat 2710387, Latte with non-dairy milk 2710388, Cappuccino 2710472 all list 36); the third-party mirror used for this record did not display caffeine. Caffeine per drink depends on shots: Starbucks grande latte (2 shots) = 150 mg/473 mL (~32 mg/100 mL); a 240 mL café latte with a double shot is ~50-60 mg/100 mL. Norway's Matvaretabellen 'caffe latte, single, whole milk' lists 59 kcal, 3.1 g protein, 3.2 g fat per 100 g (whole milk version).

name: Caffè Latte (skim/nonfat milk)
notes: FNDDS 'Coffee, Latte, nonfat'. Density 1.03 g/mL. Same caffeine caveats as Caffè Latte.

name: Caffè Latte (plant milk)
notes: FNDDS 'Coffee, Latte, with non-dairy milk' (generic plant milk blend). Oat-milk lattes are higher in carbs/kcal, almond lower; for precision, build as espresso + the specific plant milk entry. Density 1.02 g/mL.

name: Cappuccino
notes: FNDDS 'Coffee, Cappuccino' (unsweetened; recipe has more foam/air and less milk per gram than latte). Density 1.02 g/mL (foam lowers it; approximate). Traditional Italian cappuccino ~150-180 mL; US chains 240-590 mL. Starbucks grande cappuccino = 150 mg caffeine.

name: Flat White

source.name: Matvaretabellen (Norwegian Food Composition Table) 'Caffe latte, single, with whole milk' for nutrients; Starbucks published caffeine

notes: No USDA record. A flat white is espresso (often ristretto) with steamed whole milk and thin microfoam, so macros use Norway's whole-milk latte record (EuroFIR recipe calculation; 59 kcal/100 g), density 1.03. Caffeine default = Starbucks grande flat white 195 mg/473 mL (41 mg/100 mL); a classic 160-180 mL Australian/UK flat white with a double shot (~130-150 mg) is ~75-85 mg/100 mL, hence the wide range. Starbucks lists ~220 kcal/17 g sugar/150 mg sodium per grande (lower kcal per mL than the Norwegian record).

name: Caffè Mocha
notes: FNDDS 'Coffee, Cafe Mocha' (espresso, milk, chocolate syrup; no whipped cream). Density 1.05 g/mL (sugar-rich). Whipped cream adds ~70-100 kcal per drink - offer as a modifier. Caffeine includes a little from cocoa.

name: Espresso Macchiato
notes: FNDDS 'Coffee, macchiato' = espresso 'marked' with a little milk foam (not the large sweet 'latte macchiato' sold by chains; for Starbucks Caramel Macchiato use the latte + syrup modifier).

name: Instant Coffee (made with water)
notes: USDA SR 'coffee, instant, regular, prepared with water'. Powder (FDC 171893) contains 3140 mg caffeine/100 g (~31 mg per gram), so 1-2 rounded tsp (~1.8-3.6 g) in 240 mL gives ~24-47 mg/100 mL. UK/AU mugs are usually 250-350 mL.

name: Instant Decaf Coffee
notes: USDA SR 'coffee, instant, decaffeinated, prepared with water'.

name: Frozen Blended Coffee (frappé)
notes: FNDDS 'Frozen coffee drink' (sweetened, without whipped cream). Chain recipes vary a lot (Starbucks Frappuccino grande ~230-400 kcal). Density 1.05 g/mL.

name: Bottled/Canned Coffee Drink (milk, sweetened)
notes: FNDDS 'Coffee, bottled/canned' (milk-based, sweetened, e.g., bottled Frappuccino-type). Brand caffeine varies (~90-225 mg per bottle); use brand label if known.

name: Cuban Coffee (café cubano, sweetened espresso)
notes: FNDDS 'Coffee, Cuban' = espresso whipped with sugar (espumita). Small serving, very high caffeine per mL.

name: Black Tea (brewed)
notes: USDA SR 'tea, black, brewed, prepared with tap water' (~47 mg caffeine per 8 oz). Chin et al. 2008 (J Anal Toxicol 32:702) measured 14-61 mg caffeine per 6- or 8-oz serving across 20 white, green and black teas (~6-36 mg/100 mL), with no consistent trend by tea type; steep time mattered more. UK CoFID weak black tea infusion lists ~18 mg potassium/100 g, so potassium varies with strength. Milk is a modifier (UK default often includes milk).

name: Decaf Black Tea
notes: USDA SR decaffeinated brewed black tea. Chin et al. 2008: decaf teas contained <12 mg per serving (<5 mg/100 mL).

name: Green Tea (brewed)
notes: USDA SR 'tea, green, brewed, regular' (~28 mg per 8 oz). Chin et al. 2008 (J Anal Toxicol 32:702) measured 14-61 mg caffeine per 6- or 8-oz serving across 20 white, green and black teas (~6-36 mg/100 mL), with no consistent trend by tea type; steep time mattered more. Japanese Standard Tables list sencha infusion at 20 mg/100 mL and gyokuro at 160 mg/100 mL (via secondary summary), showing how much leaf type and dose matter.

name: Oolong Tea (brewed)
notes: USDA SR 'tea, Oolong, brewed'. Chin et al. 2008 (J Anal Toxicol 32:702) measured 14-61 mg caffeine per 6- or 8-oz serving across 20 white, green and black teas (~6-36 mg/100 mL), with no consistent trend by tea type; steep time mattered more.

name: White Tea (brewed)

source.name: Proxy: USDA brewed green tea (FDC 171917); caffeine range from Chin et al. 2008

notes: No USDA record for white tea. Nutrients are negligible like other plain teas, so green tea values are used as a proxy. The popular claim that white tea is always lowest in caffeine is not supported: Chin et al. 2008 found no consistent trend by tea type (14-61 mg per serving overall).

name: Matcha (whisked with water)

source.name: Japan Standard Tables of Food Composition (MEXT) matcha powder caffeine 3.2 g/100 g, via secondary summaries; derived per 100 mL

notes: Derived: 2 g matcha powder (~64 mg caffeine at 32 mg/g) whisked into 240 mL water = 26.7 mg/100 mL. Published per-gram values span ~19-44 mg/g and doses span 1-4 g, and traditional usucha uses ~2 g in only ~70 mL (~90 mg/100 mL), hence the wide range. Energy/protein/potassium of the powder are small (~2 g of powder per cup) but were not verified from a primary table, so they are null. Matcha lattes: build as matcha + milk modifier.

name: Herbal Tea (generic, e.g., peppermint)
notes: USDA SR 'tea, herb, other than chamomile, brewed'. Caffeine-free (Chin et al. 2008 detected no caffeine in herbal teas). Note: yerba mate and guayusa are NOT caffeine-free and should not use this entry.

name: Chamomile Tea
notes: USDA SR 'tea, herb, brewed, chamomile'. Caffeine-free.

name: Rooibos Tea

source.name: Proxy: USDA herbal tea other than chamomile (FDC 173232)

notes: No dedicated USDA record. Rooibos (Aspalathus linearis) is naturally caffeine-free; nutrients of the plain infusion are negligible, so the generic herbal tea record is used.

name: Hibiscus Tea
notes: USDA SR 'tea, hibiscus, brewed'. Caffeine-free. Agua de jamaica is usually sweetened - add a sugar modifier.

name: Iced Tea (brewed, sweetened / sweet tea)
notes: FNDDS 'Tea, iced, brewed, black, pre-sweetened with sugar' (32 kcal/100 g; the mirror used did not display caffeine). Caffeine is estimated from USDA brewed black tea (20 mg/100 g) scaled for the ~8% sugar dilution (~18 mg/100 mL), so treat it as approximate; restaurant iced tea is often brewed weaker or diluted by ice (USDA Wendy's unsweetened iced tea: 8 mg/100 g). Southern US sweet tea can be sweeter than this record.

name: Iced Tea (brewed, unsweetened)

source.name: USDA FoodData Central (SR Legacy, restaurant iced tea)

notes: USDA SR 'WENDY'S, tea, ready-to-drink, unsweetened' - a restaurant brewed iced tea. Home-brewed iced tea can be stronger (up to brewed black tea, 20 mg/100 mL).

name: Bottled Iced Tea (black, sweetened)
notes: USDA SR 'tea, black, ready-to-drink, lemon, sweetened'. Brands vary from ~20 to ~45 kcal/100 mL; diet versions ~0 kcal (SR 171892).

name: Bottled Green Tea (sweetened)
notes: USDA SR 'tea, green, ready-to-drink, sweetened'. Unsweetened bottled green tea: ~0 kcal, 12 mg caffeine/100 g (SR 171911).

name: Chai Tea Latte

source.name: Starbucks published nutrition (grande Chai Tea Latte, 2% milk), via secondary listings

notes: Per grande (473 mL) with 2% milk: 240 kcal, 42 g sugar, 8 g protein, 4.5 g fat, 95 mg caffeine. Chai concentrates are heavily sweetened, so this is a coffee-shop default; unsweetened homemade masala chai is closer to black tea + milk. Sodium and potassium not verified (null).

name: Bubble Tea / Boba Milk Tea
notes: FNDDS 'Tea, bubble (bubble tea)' (55 kcal/100 g, most carbs from tapioca starch; density 1.04). Shop drinks are often much sweeter: Min, Green & Kim 2017 (Food Sci Nutr 5:38) and menus report ~260-300 kcal and ~38 g sugar per 16 oz boba milk tea (~8 g sugar/100 mL). Note the tapioca pearls are eaten, not drunk - the hydration agent may want to discount them. Caffeine depends on tea base and was not available from the record (null).

name: Red Bull Energy Drink

source.name: Red Bull label (redbull.com) + USDA SR Red Bull (FDC 173210) for water/protein/potassium

notes: Label per 8.4 fl oz (250 mL) can: 110 kcal, 27 g sugar, ~105 mg sodium (retailer labels 101-105), 80 mg caffeine (32 mg/100 mL, same per mL across can sizes). USDA SR per 100 g: 43 kcal, 10.2 g sugar, 29 mg caffeine (density ~1.045 g/mL -> ~30 mg/100 mL), consistent. EU can is also 250 mL.

name: Red Bull Sugarfree
notes: USDA SR Red Bull sugar-free (per 100 g, density ~1.00). Caffeine set to the label's 80 mg per 250 mL (SR: 30 mg/100 g). Red Bull Zero is similar.

name: Monster Energy (original green)

source.name: Monster label (via US retailer listings) + USDA SR Monster (FDC 171935)

notes: Label per 16 fl oz (473 mL) can: 230 kcal (older labels 210), 58 g carbs, 54 g sugar, 370 mg sodium, 160 mg caffeine (~34 mg/100 mL). USDA SR per 100 g: 47 kcal, 10.9 g sugar, 77 mg sodium, 33 mg caffeine - consistent. UK/EU Monster is a 500 mL can at the same 32 mg/100 mL legal-labelling range ('high caffeine content' warning above 150 mg/L).

name: Monster Lo-Carb / zero-sugar Monster
notes: USDA SR 'MONSTER energy drink, low carb' (~140 mg per 16 oz). Monster Zero Ultra is similar in caffeine (~140-150 mg/can per label); verify per flavor.

name: Celsius (original sparkling)
notes: Label per 12 fl oz (355 mL) can: 10 kcal, 0 g sugar, ~0-5 mg sodium, 200 mg caffeine (56 mg/100 mL - nearly double Red Bull per mL). Carbohydrate (sweetened with erythritol/sucralose) and potassium not verified -> null. Celsius Essentials 16 oz = 270 mg; label says do not exceed 2 cans/day.

name: Bang Energy
notes: Label per 16 fl oz can: 0 kcal, 0 g sugar, 3 g carbs, 40 mg sodium, 85-120 mg potassium (flavor dependent; 85 used), 300 mg caffeine (63 mg/100 mL). One can approaches the FDA's 400 mg/day adult guidance. 'Ghost-type' high-caffeine drinks: see separate entry.

name: Ghost Energy
notes: Label per 16 fl oz can: 5-10 kcal (flavor dependent), 0 g sugar, 30 mg sodium, 200 mg caffeine (42 mg/100 mL). Similar zero-sugar 200 mg/16 oz drinks (C4 Energy, Alani Nu, Reign ~300 mg) can be logged with this or a custom caffeine value.

name: 5-hour Energy Shot

source.name: Manufacturer/retailer caffeine disclosures; Consumer Reports 2012 test (via Caffeine Informer)

notes: 1.93 fl oz (57 mL) shot. Regular ~200 mg caffeine (351 mg/100 mL); Extra Strength 230 mg (404 mg/100 mL). A 2012 Consumer Reports test measured 215 mg (regular) and 242 mg (Extra Strength). Volume is tiny, so it contributes almost nothing to hydration but a lot to caffeine. Other nutrients not verified -> null.

name: Rockstar Energy (original)
notes: USDA SR 'Energy drink, ROCKSTAR' converted with density 1.045 g/mL (~163 mg caffeine per 16 oz, matching the 160 mg label).

name: Energy Drink (generic, sugared)
notes: USDA SR 'Energy Drink with carbonated water and high fructose corn syrup' - fallback for unlisted sugared brands. Brand range 30-35 mg caffeine/100 mL is typical; use the label if known.

name: Energy Drink (generic, sugar-free)
notes: USDA SR 'Energy Drink, sugar free' - fallback for unlisted zero-sugar brands. Newer 'performance' brands run 42-63 mg/100 mL (Ghost, Celsius, Bang).

name: Gatorade Thirst Quencher

source.name: PepsiCo Gatorade nutrition sheet (20 fl oz Lemon-Lime) + USDA SR Gatorade G (FDC 173660) for water/carbs

notes: Label per 20 fl oz (591 mL): 140 kcal, 34 g sugar, 270 mg sodium, 80 mg potassium (per 100 mL: 23.7 kcal, 5.8 g sugar, 45.7 mg Na). Carbohydrate from USDA SR (6.43 g/100 g x 1.03 g/mL); labels round total carbs. Classic ~6% carbohydrate isotonic formula. Gatorade Zero/G2: see G2 entry.

name: Gatorade G2 (lower sugar)
notes: USDA SR 'Gatorade G2, low calorie'. Same electrolytes as regular Gatorade with ~1/4 of the sugar.

name: Powerade

source.name: Powerade label (20 fl oz Mountain Berry Blast, via US retailer listings)

notes: Current label per 20 fl oz: 130 kcal, 34 g sugar, 400 mg sodium, 130 mg potassium (per 100 mL: 22 kcal, 5.75 g sugar, 67.7 mg Na). Powerade's sodium was raised in recent reformulations; the older USDA SR record (FDC 175108) lists 42 mg Na/100 g - don't use it for sodium. Total carbohydrate not verified for this formula -> null.

name: Powerade Zero
notes: USDA SR 'Powerade Zero Ion4'. Current Powerade Zero labels may list higher sodium after reformulation - verify on the bottle.

name: BODYARMOR SuperDrink

source.name: BODYARMOR label (16 fl oz Strawberry Banana, via US retailer listing)

notes: One coherent label used (Strawberry Banana, 16 fl oz): 110 kcal, 29 g carbs/sugar, 30 mg sodium, 680 mg potassium. Across flavors: 110-120 kcal, 25-29 g sugar, 30-40 mg Na, 680-700 mg K. Note the electrolyte profile is potassium-heavy and LOW in sodium (unlike Gatorade/ORS). BODYARMOR LYTE: ~20 kcal per 16 oz, 700 mg K.

name: Pedialyte Classic (oral electrolyte solution)

source.name: Abbott Nutrition, Pedialyte Classic product information

notes: Abbott per 1 L (most flavors): 70 kcal, 19 g carbs, 13 g sugar, 1080 mg sodium (~47 mEq/L), 780 mg potassium (~20 mEq/L), 1240 mg chloride. Per 12 fl oz: 25 kcal, 390 mg Na, 280 mg K. One flavor lists 1030 mg Na/25 g sugar per L. AdvancedCare Plus has more sodium (60 mEq/L).

name: Oral Rehydration Solution (WHO formula)

source.name: WHO/UNICEF reduced-osmolarity ORS composition (WHO Drug Information 16(2), 2002)

notes: Per litre: sodium 75 mmol (1725 mg), potassium 20 mmol (782 mg), chloride 65 mmol, citrate 10 mmol, anhydrous glucose 75 mmol (13.5 g); 245 mOsm/L. Energy computed at 4 kcal/g glucose. Sachet ORS made up per instructions (e.g., Dioralyte in the UK uses a different, lower-sodium recipe - check the pack).

name: Liquid I.V. Hydration Multiplier (mixed)
notes: One 16 g stick in 16 fl oz (473 mL) water (~485 mL total). Per stick: 45-50 kcal, 11 g sugar, 500-560 mg sodium, ~370 mg potassium (flavor dependent). Per-100 mL values assume the label dilution; users who mix into a different volume should be offered 'per stick' logging. Sugar-free version: ~0 g sugar, similar electrolytes. LMNT/DripDrop-type mixes: log via custom entry (LMNT ~1000 mg Na per stick).

name: Prime Hydration

source.name: Prime Hydration label (16.9 fl oz, via US retailer listings)

notes: Per 16.9 fl oz (500 mL): 20-25 kcal, 10-20 mg sodium (500 mL UK/EU variants list ~30 mg), 700 mg potassium; caffeine-free (do NOT confuse with Prime Energy, 200 mg caffeine/12 oz). Like BODYARMOR, very low sodium - a weak sweat-replacement drink despite the marketing. Sugar/carb split not verified -> null.

name: Propel Fitness Water (zero)
notes: USDA SR 'Propel Zero, fruit-flavored, non-carbonated'. Overlaps with Part A 'water variants'; kept here as an electrolyte water.

name: Soy Milk (unsweetened)
notes: USDA Foundation 'Soy milk, unsweetened, plain, shelf stable' (analytical data). Total sugars not declared; sucrose 0.56 g/100 g was the only sugar detected, used here. Density 1.03 g/mL. Calcium 101 mg/100 g (fortified). Sweetened 'original' soy milk is ~50-55 kcal/100 mL with ~5-6 g sugar per cup more.

name: Almond Milk (unsweetened)
notes: USDA SR 'almond milk, unsweetened, shelf stable'. Density 1.01 g/mL. Very low protein (0.4 g/100 mL vs ~3.4 for cow's milk).

name: Almond Milk (sweetened, vanilla)
notes: USDA SR 'almond milk, sweetened, vanilla flavor, ready-to-drink'. Density 1.02 g/mL.

name: Almond Milk (chocolate)
notes: USDA SR 'almond milk, chocolate, ready-to-drink'. Trace caffeine from cocoa not reported (0 in record).

name: Oat Milk (unsweetened/plain)
notes: USDA Foundation 'Oat milk, unsweetened, plain, refrigerated'. Total sugars not declared; sum of measured sugars (glucose 0.77 + maltose 1.55 g/100 g) used. 'Unsweetened' oat milk still contains sugars formed when oat starch is enzymatically broken down. Density 1.03 g/mL.

name: Oat Milk (Oatly Original type)

source.name: Oatly US product page (Oatmilk Original, per 1 cup / 240 mL)

notes: Label per 1 cup (240 mL): 120 kcal, 5 g fat, 16 g carbs, 7 g sugars (formed from oats, labelled as added sugars), 100 mg sodium. Protein and potassium not captured from the page -> null. Barista editions are higher in fat (~140 kcal/cup).

name: Coconut Milk Beverage (unsweetened, carton)

source.name: So Delicious Organic Unsweetened Coconutmilk Beverage label (via retailer listings)

notes: Per cup: 45 kcal, 4.5 g fat (mostly saturated), 1 g carbs, 0 g sugar, 25 mg sodium (shelf-stable version lists 10 mg). This is the dilute carton beverage - NOT canned coconut milk (~170-200 kcal/100 mL) or coconut water.

name: Coconut Milk Beverage (sweetened)
notes: USDA SR 'coconut milk, sweetened, fortified with calcium, vitamins A, B12, D2' (carton beverage). Density 1.01 g/mL.

name: Rice Milk
notes: USDA SR 'rice milk, unsweetened'. Even unsweetened rice milk has ~5 g sugar/100 g from starch hydrolysis. Density 1.02 g/mL. UK FSA advises against rice milk for children under 5 (inorganic arsenic).

name: Pea Milk (original)

source.name: Ripple Foods product page (Original, per 8 fl oz)

notes: Ripple Original per 8 fl oz: 100 kcal, 8 g protein (similar to cow's milk), 4.5 g fat, 160 mg sodium, 440 mg calcium. Carbohydrate/sugar for Original (sweetened) and potassium not verified -> null; Unsweetened Original is ~80 kcal with 0 g sugar per brand listings. No USDA record found for pea milk.

name: Beer (regular lager, ~5% ABV)
notes: USDA SR 'beer, regular, all'. Alcohol 3.9 g/100 g x density 1.01 = 3.94 g/100 mL = 5.0% ABV. A 12 oz (355 mL) can = 14.0 g ethanol = exactly 1 US standard drink (NIAAA, 14 g) = 1.8 UK units (8 g). Servings: US can 355 mL, US pint 473 mL, UK pint 568 mL, EU 330/500 mL.

name: Light Beer (~4% ABV)
notes: USDA SR 'beer, light' (3.1 g alcohol/100 g = ~3.9% ABV; ~103 kcal per 12 oz). Bud Light record (FDC 169572) is 3.3 g/100 g = 4.2% ABV. NIAAA notes many light beers have almost as much alcohol as regular beer.

name: Craft IPA (~6.7% ABV)

source.name: Sierra Nevada Hazy Little Thing IPA official nutrition (12 oz)

notes: Representative craft IPA: Sierra Nevada Hazy Little Thing, 6.7% ABV, 214 kcal, 20.6 g carbs, 2.2 g protein per 12 oz. Ethanol = 6.7% x 0.789 = 5.29 g/100 mL -> 18.8 g per 12 oz = 1.3 US standard drinks; a 16 oz pour = 1.8. IPAs commonly range 5.5-7.5% ABV; double/imperial IPAs 8-10% (use the strong-beer entry). NIAAA: some craft beers reach 10% ABV (2 standard drinks per 12 oz). Sugar/sodium/potassium not published -> null.

name: Strong Craft Beer / Double IPA (~9-10% ABV)
notes: USDA SR 'beer, higher alcohol': 7.7 g alcohol/100 g -> 7.78 g/100 mL = 9.9% ABV. The record's very low carbohydrate (0.27 g) and modest kcal look inconsistent with typical double IPAs/stouts (Sierra Nevada Big Little Thing: 9.5% ABV, 254 kcal per 12 oz); treat kcal/carbs as uncertain, ABV as the key field.

name: Non-alcoholic Beer
notes: USDA SR 'Malt beverage, includes non-alcoholic beer' (0.3 g alcohol/100 g, ~0.4% ABV; US 'non-alcoholic' means <0.5% ABV). This record is a sweet malt beverage; modern NA craft beers (e.g., Athletic Brewing) are often ~50-70 kcal per 12 oz with less sugar.

name: Hard Seltzer (5% ABV)

source.name: White Claw label (12 oz, via US retailer listings); FNDDS Hard seltzer (FDC 2710622) cross-check

notes: White Claw per 12 oz: 100 kcal, 2 g carbs/sugar, 20 mg sodium, 5% ABV -> 3.95 g ethanol/100 mL, 14.0 g per can = 1 US standard drink. FNDDS 'Hard seltzer' (24 kcal, 0.55 g carbs, 17 mg Na, 6 mg K, 3.2 g alcohol per 100 g ~= 4% ABV) is a lighter generic; potassium taken from it. Many brands also sell 8% versions (e.g., White Claw Surge) - use a custom ABV.

name: Hard Cider (~5% ABV)
notes: USDA SR 'AMBER, hard cider' (4.0 g alcohol/100 g -> ~5.1% ABV). Sweetness varies widely by brand (dry ciders ~1-3 g sugar/100 mL, sweet US ciders up to ~6-7). UK ciders range 4-7.5% ABV.

name: Red Wine
notes: USDA SR 'wine, table, red': 10.6 g alcohol/100 g x density 0.993 = 10.5 g/100 mL = 13.3% ABV. A US 5 oz (148 mL) pour = 15.6 g ethanol = 1.1 US standard drinks (NIAAA's 1 drink assumes 12% ABV). UK: 175 mL at 13% = 2.3 units; servings 125/175/250 mL. Varietal records (Cabernet, Merlot, Pinot Noir) are similar.

name: White Wine
notes: USDA SR 'wine, table, white': 10.3 g alcohol/100 g x 0.993 = 10.2 g/100 mL = ~13.0% ABV. Sweet/late-harvest whites have more sugar (SR 173202). UK 175 mL glass at 12% = 2.1 units.

name: Rosé Wine
notes: USDA SR 'wine, rose' (9.6 g alcohol/100 g -> ~12.1% ABV). Dry Provence-style rosés have less sugar than this average.

name: Sparkling Wine (Champagne/Prosecco/Cava)
notes: FNDDS 'Wine, sparkling' (9.5 g alcohol/100 g -> ~12.0% ABV; FNDDS '1 glass' = 180 g). Typical flute ~120-150 mL. Sweetness labels (Brut Nature < 3 g/L sugar up to Doux > 50 g/L) change sugar substantially.

name: Spirits, 40% ABV (vodka, gin, rum, whiskey, tequila)
notes: USDA SR 'distilled, all (gin, rum, vodka, whiskey) 80 proof': 33.4 g alcohol/100 g x density 0.948 (40% ethanol-water) = 31.7 g/100 mL = 40% ABV. US shot 1.5 fl oz (44 mL) = 13.9 g = 1 US standard drink; UK single 25 mL = 1 unit (7.9 g), larger UK measure 35 mL; a US 'double' 3 fl oz. All energy is from ethanol (~7 kcal/g). Higher-proof spirits: scale alcohol by ABV (86 proof SR 171919, 100 proof SR 173664).

name: Gin & Tonic

source.name: Composite from USDA SR: 1.5 fl oz 80-proof gin (FDC 174815) + 4 fl oz tonic water (FDC 171869)

notes: Recipe: 44 mL gin (40%) + 118 mL tonic, ice melt ignored (~163 mL). Per drink ~139 kcal, 10.7 g sugar, 14.0 g ethanol (1 US standard drink). Bar pours vary (UK single 25 mL + 150-200 mL tonic is ~1 unit, ~3% ABV); slimline tonic removes the sugar. Canned G&Ts run 5-7% ABV (CSPI alcohol chart lists Cutwater G&T 6.2% ABV, 230 kcal).

name: Rum & Cola (Cuba Libre)

source.name: Composite from USDA SR: 1.5 fl oz 80-proof rum (FDC 174815) + 4 fl oz cola (FDC 174852)

notes: Recipe: 44 mL rum (40%) + 118 mL regular cola (~163 mL). Per drink ~149 kcal, ~12.2 g sugar, 14.0 g ethanol (1 US standard drink), ~11 mg caffeine from the cola. Diet cola removes nearly all sugar; same template works for whiskey & cola or vodka & soda (use club soda: 0 kcal).

name: Margarita
notes: FNDDS 'Margarita' (1 drink = 225 g; 8.2 g alcohol/100 g -> ~8.4 g/100 mL, ~10.7% ABV; density 1.03 assumed). One FNDDS drink holds ~18.5 g ethanol = 1.3 US standard drinks. High sodium reflects the salted rim. Restaurant/frozen margaritas are often larger (12-20 oz) and can contain 2-3 standard drinks; a classic 3-oz-pour on the rocks is smaller but stronger.

name: Piña Colada
notes: USDA SR 'pina colada, prepared-from-recipe' (9.9 g alcohol/100 g; density 1.05 assumed -> ~10.4 g/100 mL, ~13% ABV). Very energy-dense (~435 kcal per 8 oz).

name: Whiskey Sour
notes: USDA SR 'whiskey sour' (14.1 g alcohol/100 g; density 1.02 assumed -> ~14.4 g/100 mL, ~18% ABV). Sugars field uses carbohydrate (sugar not separately reported; it is essentially all sugar from sour mix).

name: Flavored Malt Beverage / Hard Lemonade
notes: USDA SR 'malt beer, hard lemonade' (~5.2% ABV). NIAAA notes flavored malt beverages are often ~7% ABV (8-10 oz = 1 standard drink); 'Twisted Tea'/'Mike's Harder' variants reach 8%.

name: Non-alcoholic Wine
notes: USDA SR 'Wine, non-alcoholic'. Many dealcoholised wines contain up to 0.5% ABV and added grape juice (more sugar than this record).

name: Kombucha
notes: FNDDS 'Tea, kombucha' (16 kcal, 4 g sugar per 100 g). Cross-check GT's Synergy labels: 50-60 kcal and 12-16 g sugar per 16 oz (~2.5-3.4 g sugar/100 mL). Caffeine (residual from the tea base, partly consumed in fermentation) is not reported -> null. Commercial 'non-alcoholic' kombucha must stay <0.5% ABV in the US; some raw/'hard' kombuchas are 3-7% ABV (log those as alcohol).

name: Chicken Broth
notes: USDA SR 'Soup, chicken broth, ready-to-serve'. Density taken as 1.00 (USDA's 1 cup = 249 g would imply ~1.05). Very high sodium (~890 mg per cup); reduced-sodium broth (FDC 172888) ~231 mg/100 g; bone broths have more protein (~4-10 g per cup by brand). Brothy soups can use this entry; chunky soups should not be logged as drinks.

name: Hot Chocolate (made with milk)
notes: USDA SR 'Milk, chocolate beverage, hot cocoa, homemade'. Density 1.05 g/mL. ~5 mg caffeine per cup from cocoa. Coffee-shop hot chocolates with whipped cream are richer (Starbucks grande ~370-400 kcal).

name: Hot Cocoa (mix made with water)
notes: USDA SR 'Cocoa mix, powder, prepared with water'. Density 1.04 g/mL.

name: Vegetable Juice (tomato-based, V8-type)

source.name: Campbell's V8 Original 100% Vegetable Juice label

notes: V8 Original per 8 fl oz: 45 kcal, 9 g carbs, 7 g sugars (no added sugar), 640 mg sodium. Low Sodium V8 is ~140 mg Na per 8 oz. Protein and potassium not captured from the label (V8 is potassium-rich; Low Sodium V8 advertises more potassium) -> null. POSSIBLE OVERLAP with Part A juices - de-duplicate on merge.

name: Apple Cider Vinegar Drink (ready-to-drink)

source.name: Bragg Refreshers ACV Ginger Lemon Honey label (via retailer listing)

notes: Per 8 fl oz: 40 kcal, 9 g added sugar, 10 mg sodium. DIY: 2 tbsp Bragg ACV-honey blend in 8 oz water = 35 kcal, 10 g sugar per glass (~267 mL). Plain ACV (1 tbsp) in water adds ~3 kcal and negligible sugar. Shrubs/drinking vinegars (e.g., Pok Pok Som) are concentrates - log diluted volume. No national-database record exists.
